newsitem.title: POLAND: Asia, Europe investors buy Optimus bonds.
newsitem.headline: Asia, Europe investors buy Optimus bonds.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA's 300 international convertible bonds at a par value of $100,000 each have been placed with financial investors from Asia and Europe, the firm said in a statement on Tuesday.
"We have been informed by the underwriter of the issue that Optimus SA convertible bonds were placed among financial investors from Asia and Europe," the statement said.
"At the present time the firm Microsoft is not among the group of investors," the statement said, adding that Optimus' cooperation with Microsoft since 1991 was systematically growing to new areas.
Optimus has said it would use some of the issue's funds to launch mass production of its new computer produced in cooperation with Microsoft.
Earlier this month the firm announced it had received orders to convert into shares 159 out of its 300 convertible bonds, a move it expected to boost January pre-tax profit by 1.3 million zlotys.
It said the orders were made by the underwriters of the five-year $30 million bond issue with Merrill Lynch International ordering 109 bonds converted and Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA 50.
The bonds are exchangeable into 6,947 common shares at $14.76 a share. Optimus closed on the Warsaw bourse on Tuesday at 125 zlotys.
The registration of shares from the conversion of the 159 bonds would bring the number of Optimus outstanding shares to 5,511,528 million from the current 4,406,955.
The conversion of all the bonds and their registration in court would bring the firm's number of shares outstanding to 6,484,108.
